 Order No. 02 Dated: 12.09.2023

The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the concerned respondents to
pay the amount of compensation to the extent of the petitioner's share with respect to the land
appertaining to Khata No. 36, Plot No. 1000, measuring an area of 1.46 acres of Mouza-Bank,
Thana-Mohanpur, District-Deoghar acquired for construction of Punasi Main Canal, Deoghar.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is one of the descendants of the recorded raiyat of the aforesaid land which has been acquired for construction of Punasi Main Canal, Deoghar.

In the said process, Land Acquisition Case No. 69/2020-21 (wrongly mentioned as Land Acquisition Case No. 68/2020-21 in paragraph-5 of the present writ petition) was initiated and an award of Rs.70,13,912/- was prepared in favour of the concerned raiyats including the petitioner.

The said fact would be evident from the notice issued by the respondent no. 5 - the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Medium Irrigation Project, Deoghar under Section 37(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Annexure-1 to the writ petition).

sentences.text:
It is further submitted that though some of awardees/co- raiyats have been paid compensation,
however, the petitioner has not been paid any compensation.
She represented the respondent nos. 4 and 5 raising the said grievance, however, the same remained unresponded, which has compelled her to prefer the present writ petition.

4. Mrs. Shalini Shahdeo, AC to SC (L&C)-I appearing on behalf of the respondents, submits that the aforesaid claim of the petitioner is required to be factually examined by the respondent no. 5 and hence, if the petitioner prefers a fresh representation before the said respondent, an appropriate decision in accordance with law will be taken.

5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the nature of the prayer made in the present writ petition, without entering into the merit of the petitioner's aforesaid claim, she is given liberty to prefer a fresh representation before the respondent no. 5 in this regard.

On receipt of the said representation, the respondent no. 5, after providing an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner and on verifying the relevant records, shall take an appropriate informed decision within six weeks from the date of filing of the said representation.
6. The present writ petition is accordingly disposed of with aforesaid liberty and direction.

(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Manish Manki Devi vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119032595/
